Leaders agree on trade deal

By Jane Reporter

Leaders from twelve countries agreed on Sunday to cut tariffs on farm goods and machinery, ending two years of talks that had stalled several times over subsidies and market access.

The agreement, signed in the early hours after an all-night session, phases in the cuts over five years and sets up a joint committee to settle disputes between members.

Officials said the deal would lift trade between the members by about a fifth by the end of the decade, though independent economists cautioned that the gains depend on how quickly the cuts take effect.

Farm groups in several countries criticised the speed of the talks and said they had not been consulted on the final text, which runs to more than four hundred pages.

The deal still needs to be ratified by each country's parliament, a process expected to take most of next year.
